compare.br: In Brazil, people say “Que calor!” or “Tá chovendo” and use Celsius: 30 degrees is a hot day.
compare.us: In the USA, people use Fahrenheit: 85 degrees is hot and 30 degrees is very cold. Chicago has hot summers and snowy winters.
compare.tip: Do not worry about the numbers. Say hot, warm, cool or cold.

pages.title: Four seasons, one city · 1/3
paragraphs: Hello from **Chicago**! I live here, and the weather is always a topic. People say, “**Nice day, huh?**” in the elevator, at the bus stop and in the café.
In **summer**, it is very hot and sunny. We go to the lake and eat ice cream. In **autumn**, it is cool and windy. The trees are red and yellow. Chicago has a nickname: the Windy City.
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: Four seasons, one city · 2/3
paragraphs: In **winter**, it is freezing! There is a lot of snow, and I say, “**Brr! Bundle up.**” I wear a warm coat, a hat and gloves. When it is pouring rain, I bring an umbrella. **It’s freezing out there!**

In **spring**, the days are warm again. Flowers come out, and the birds sing. Last week, I listened to “The Four Seasons” by Antonio Vivaldi. It is a famous piece of music from Italy, from about 1725. It has one part for each season. In the spring part, you can hear birds.

pages.title: Four seasons, one city · 3/3
paragraphs: Which season do you like? I like spring, but my friend Evan likes snow. He says, “**I need a warm coat**,” and then he laughs. Write soon, and **stay warm**!

pages.title: Som e ritmo
pairs: Em "isn't it?" a voz sobe um pouco, pedindo concordância. Nice e MOR são fortes.
It's very soa "it-sve-ri". A sílaba forte de very é a primeira.
Bata NEED, WARM, COAT. I e a ficam fracos: "ai-NEED-a-WARM-COAT".
